findings.issue: Only the Helm chart protects auth (values.yaml:140 sets framework). auth's application.yml sets no default for server.forward-headers-strategy. Any Kubernetes deploy of auth without that env would get Boot's deduced NATIVE strategy. The @ConditionalOnProperty filter would then not register, and Tomcat's RemoteIpValve would turn a client X-Forwarded-For from an internal-range peer into getRemoteAddr(). That breaks the ClientIp fallback the ADR's trust-boundary bullet relies on. The current chart is correct, so this is a defence-in-depth gap and not reachable today.
findings.fix: Pin a safe default in auth's application.yml, for example `server.forward-headers-strategy: ${SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY:none}`, matching what user-service does. Helm keeps overriding it to framework. Optionally also update docs/guides/deploy-aws.md:195 ('The gateway keeps none') to say every non-auth service runs with none.

summary: Delta 690f934a..a04ad610. The auth filter now captures getRemoteAddr, getRemoteHost and getRemotePort from the raw Tomcat request before ForwardedHeaderFilter runs. It then wraps whatever request the framework hands down in the chain lambda, so the outermost request always reports the socket peer. This holds for X-Forwarded-For and RFC 7239 Forwarded: for= in any letter case: the pinning does not depend on header names, and the tests cover lower-case XFF, upper-case FORWARDED with a bracketed v6 address, and both headers together. When no forwarded header is present, OncePerRequestFilter skips the filter and the raw peer is seen anyway. ERROR re-dispatch goes through doFilterNestedErrorDispatch and then the overridden doFilterInternal, so it is pinned too. Under framework, Boot adds no Tomcat RemoteIpValve: the valve is added only for NATIVE or when server.tomcat.remoteip.* headers are set, and the worktree sets none. The ConditionalOnProperty mirrors Boot's own condition and still binds from the SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY env var. The test asserts exactly one registration. The Helm template now emits SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none for every service except auth-service. I found no other service that sets it in values env, so there are no duplicate env entries. No non-auth service builds URLs from the request scheme or host, so dropping NATIVE costs no function. The gateway counts XFF from the right itself, and user-service's own default is also none. ADR 0002's trust-boundary bullets (lines 46-50) match the code and the chart. Round-2 minors: (1) the Forwarded: for= bypass is resolved; (2) dispatcher types REQUEST, ASYNC and ERROR and the ForwardedHeaderFilterCustomizer beans are now applied, resolved; (3) none is now the Helm default for all non-auth services, resolved. The delta adds no endpoints, secrets, PII logging, ledger changes or dependencies. I am approving with one minor hardening finding.
